question: Give a detailed introduction to the Holy Quran.
answer: The word "Quran" literally means "to read" or "the book read". In Islamic terminology, the Holy Quran stands for the speech of Allah revealed on the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), the last of all Prophets, through the angel Jibraeel (Gabriel), and written down in the book. The Holy Quran contains 30 parts (Parahs), 114 Chapters (Surahs), 558 units (Rukus) and 6236 verses (Ayat). It begins with Surah al-Fatiha and ends with Surah an-Naas. The longest surah is Surah al-Baqarah and the shortest is Surah al-Kawthar. The longest verse, containing the glory and majesty of Almighty Allah, is Ayat al-Kursi. A Surah contains a minimum of three verses. Every surah has its own theme and topic and begins with Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim except Surah al-Tawbah. "Ayat" literally means a sign or symbol; in Islamic terminology a particular phrase of the Holy Quran ended with the 'o' symbol is called an Ayat. The Quran is Allah's eternal and everlasting speech, preserved in the Preserved Tablet (Loh-e-Mahfooz), as Allah says: "Nay! This is a Glorious Quran, inscribed in Al-Lauh Al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet)" (Al-Burooj: 21-22). It was revealed to the earth in two stages: first, it was revealed wholly in "Bait al-Izzat" (the nearest heaven of the world), and second, the angel Jibraeel brought its verses and chapters to the Holy Prophet gradually, as and when needed, over a period of twenty-two years and a few months — twelve years and a few months in Makkah before the migration and the rest in Madinah after the migration. On the basis of revelation, the surahs are classified into Makki (88 surahs revealed before migration) and Madani (26 surahs revealed after migration). The Holy Quran also has several qualitative names such as Al-Quran, Al-Furqan, Al-Zikr, Al-Kitab, Al-Huda, Al-Noor, Al-Haqq, Al-Shifaa' and Al-Tanzeel.
explanation: Based on the lesson's definition, statistics, revelation and naming sections (book pages 1-3, images 4-6).

question: Describe some of the merits of the Holy Quran.
answer: The Holy Quran is the last revealed book of Almighty Allah and the last message of guidance for human beings. It is a guidebook for all the nations of the world and a guarantee for success in this world and the Hereafter. There is no parallel to this great bounty of Allah: its recitation and listening are sources of reward, and its understanding and reflection upon its verses is a cause of the goodness of both worlds. Obedience to its teachings, preaching it to others, and conveying its message to people deprived of its blessings is a great virtue and a source of success in both worlds. It is a book free of any doubt — Allah says: "This is the Book (the Quran), whereof there is no doubt" (al-Baqarah: 2). It was revealed in the Arabic language so that people may understand it, and it has been read for centuries as it was read at the time of its revelation. Its greatest merit is that it is the Word of Allah; it is unique in its style, very attractive, and has great power to influence hearts, with no contradiction in its themes and meanings — which is itself evidence of its veracity. It is protected by Allah from corruption: "Verily We: It is We Who have sent down the Dhikr (the Quran) and surely, We will guard it (from corruption)" (Al-Hijr: 9). It is also a complete code of life covering the physical, spiritual, religious and worldly needs of all human beings, and a permanent and universal law.
explanation: Drawn from the "Excellence and Virtues" and "Some merits" sections (book pages 4-5, images 7-8).

question: Write down a note on the virtues of the Holy Quran.
answer: The greatest virtue of the Holy Quran is that it is the Word of Allah, free from mistake, manipulation and tampering, for as Allah is Glorious, Magnificent and free of all defects, so is His Book. It is unique in its style; it is very attractive and has great power to influence hearts, and there is no contradiction in its themes and meanings, which is evidence of its veracity. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: "The superiority of the Holy Quran over the rest of the speeches is like the superiority of Allah over the creature" (Shu'ab al-Iman, al-Baihaqi, Hadith No. 2208). The Quran is superior to all other speech just as Allah is superior to the whole of the universe. It is a book free of any doubt, and it is a complete code of life for the physical, spiritual, religious and worldly needs of all human beings — a permanent and universal law that guides us in all spheres of life. It contains guidelines about the reality of human life, lawful and unlawful, good and bad, piety and worship, and also gives Shariah rulings and principles of politics, trade, war and peace, thereby providing the means of transforming social, economic, political and moral affairs. Because of this excellence, a Muslim is required to believe in it, recite it with ablution, understand its teachings, follow them, pass them on to others, and strive for the implementation of its system in individual and social life.
explanation: Summarised from the "Excellence and Virtues of the Holy Quran" section and the rights and manners section (book pages 4-6, images 7-9).

question: Define the word "Quran".
answer: Literally, the word "Quran" means "to read" or "the book read". In Islamic terminology, the Holy Quran stands for the speech of Allah revealed on the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) through the angel Jibraeel and written down in the book.
explanation: Given in the "Introduction to the Holy Quran" definition (book page 1, image 4).

question: Define the Surah and Ayat.
answer: A Surah is a chapter of the Holy Quran which contains a minimum of three verses; every surah has its own theme and begins with Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim except Surah al-Tawbah. An Ayat literally means a sign or symbol, and in Islamic terminology a particular phrase of the Holy Quran, ended with the 'o' symbol, is called an Ayat. The Quran has 114 Surahs and 6236 Ayat.
explanation: From the definitions in the introduction section (book page 1, image 4).

question: Write down the difference between Makki and Madani Surahs.
answer: The Ayat and Surahs revealed before the migration to Madinah are called Makki (88 in number) and those revealed after the migration are called Madani (26 in number). Makki Surahs are generally shorter and mainly deal with beliefs such as the Oneness of Allah, Prophethood and the Hereafter, along with worship and the stories of previous nations and prophets; they address the believers and the polytheists and mostly use "Ya ayyuhan-nas" (O people!). Madani Surahs are longer and contain detailed Shariah rulings such as Zakat, Jihad, war and criminal laws, and also explain social, economic and domestic issues; they address the Muslims, the hypocrites and the People of the Book (Ahl-e-Kitab), and mostly use "Ya ayyuhal-lazina amanu" (O you who believe!).
explanation: Based on the characteristics of Makki and Madani Surahs (book pages 3-4, images 6-7).

question: Write down the famous names of the Holy Quran.
answer: Besides its original name "Al-Quran", the Holy Quran has several famous qualitative names mentioned in the Quran itself: Al-Quran (its original and own name), Al-Furqan (the book that differentiates between right and wrong), Al-Zikr (the book of advice), Al-Kitab (the particular book of Almighty Allah), Al-Huda (the book of guidance), Al-Noor (the book of light), Al-Haqq (the proven book, i.e. truth), Al-Shifaa' (the book which heals physical and spiritual diseases), and Al-Tanzeel (the revealed book).
explanation: From "The Names of the Holy Quran" (book pages 1-2, images 4-5).

question: Narrate at least two Ahadith regarding the virtues of the Holy Quran.
answer: First, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: "Khairukum man ta'allamal-Qur'ana wa 'allamahu" — "The best among you is he who learns the Quran and teaches it" (Sahih Bukhari, Hadith No. 5027). Second, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: "The superiority of the Holy Quran over the rest of the speeches is like the superiority of Allah over the creature" (Shu'ab al-Iman, al-Baihaqi, Hadith No. 2208). A third narration states that the Prophet left behind two things — the Holy Quran and his Sunnah — and whoever follows them will never go astray (Mustadrik Hakim, Hadith No. 4321).
explanation: The lesson quotes these Ahadith in the virtues section (book pages 4-5, image 7).

question: Describe the rights and manners of the Holy Quran.
answer: The Holy Quran is a sacred book whose glory is greater than the rest of the books, so Muslims must observe certain rights and manners regarding it: to believe in the Holy Quran; to recite it carefully with ablution; to understand its teachings and reflect on its verses; to follow its teachings; to pass on its teachings to others; and to struggle for the implementation of its system in individual and social life. Therefore we should live according to its teachings and follow them wholeheartedly.
explanation: From "The Rights and Manners regarding the Holy Quran" list (book page 6, image 9).

question: Translate the following verses. • وَآتُوا الْيَتَامَى أَمْوَالَهُمْ وَلَا تَتَبَدَّلُوا الْخَبِيثَ بِالطَّيِّبِ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ إِلَى أَمْوَالِكُمْ إِنَّهُ كَانَ حُوبًا كَبِيرًا • وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْسًا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا
answer: Translation of the first verse (Surah al-Nisa: 2): "And give unto orphans their property and do not exchange (your) bad things for (their) good ones; and devour not their substance (by adding it) to your substance. Surely, this is a great sin." Translation of the second verse (Surah al-Nisa: 4): "And give to the women (whom you marry) their Mahr (obligatory bridal money given by the husband to his wife at the time of marriage) with a good heart, but if they, of their own good pleasure, remit any part of it to you, take it, and enjoy it without fear of any harm (as Allah has made it lawful).". The first verse commands guardians to hand over to the orphans their inherited property and warns against mixing, exchanging or consuming it unjustly, declaring this a great sin. The second verse commands husbands to pay the Mahr to their wives willingly, and permits them to use whatever the wives voluntarily give up.
explanation: Translations are exactly as given in the lesson (book pages 11-12, images 14-15).

question: In the light of the verse لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ write down important types of al-Birr.
answer: Al-Birr means virtue and denotes the doing of righteous deeds; a Hadith says "Al-birru husnul-khuluq" — Birr is the name of good morals. In the light of the verse "Laisal-birra an tuwallu wujuhakum qibala al-mashriqi wal-maghrib" (al-Baqarah: 177), al-Birr is not merely turning faces towards the east or the west in prayer. The important types (components) of al-Birr mentioned in this verse are: (1) Beliefs — the one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the Angels, the Book and the Prophets; (2) Financial sacrifice — giving wealth, in spite of love for it, to the kinsfolk, the orphans, Al-Masakin (the poor), the wayfarer, and those who ask, and to set slaves free; (3) Worship — performing As-Salat (Iqamat-as-Salat) and giving the Zakat; and (4) Righteous conduct and morals — fulfilling the covenant when one makes it, and remaining patient (As-Sabirin) in extreme poverty, in ailment (disease), and at the time of fighting during battles. Those who possess these qualities are the people of truth and they are Al-Muttaqun (the pious). Hence true righteousness combines sound faith with good deeds, worship and good morals.
explanation: Verse and its explanation given in the lesson (book pages 8-9, images 11-12).

answer: النِّسَاءَ — the women. نِحْلَةً — a free gift / a bridal gift given willingly. حُوبًا — a (great) sin. بَثَّ — spread / scattered (He spread them). الْيَتَامَىٰ — the orphans.

question: In the light of the verse ...state the occasions of patience.
answer: In the verse of al-Birr (al-Baqarah: 177) the occasions of patience (Sabr) mentioned are: (i) in extreme poverty (al-Ba'sa), (ii) in ailment or disease (ad-Darra), and (iii) at the time of fighting during battles (hinal-Ba's). Those who remain patient on these three occasions are described as As-Sabirin and are counted among the people of truth and the Muttaqun.
explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Baqarah: 177 (book pages 8-9, images 11-12).

question: What does Sila-e-Rehmi means?
answer: Sila-e-Rehmi means keeping good, brotherly and cordial relations with one's blood relatives (Al-Arhaam, the plural of Rihm). The Holy Prophet (PBUH) clarified that Sila-e-Rehmi does not mean keeping relations only with relatives who are good to you, but rather keeping good relations with relatives even if they break off with you.
explanation: From the explanation of Al-Arhaam / Sila-e-Rehmi in Surah al-Nisa: 1 (book page 10, image 13).

question: What instructions are given to the guardians regarding the property of the orphans?
answer: The guardians of orphans are instructed to hand over the orphans' inherited property and wealth when they reach puberty, because their property is a trust in the guardians' hands. They must not exchange their own bad things for the orphans' good ones, must not mix or devour the orphans' wealth with their own, and must avoid wasting or consuming it unjustly. Violating the rights of orphans is a major sin and injustice in the sight of Allah (al-Nisa: 2).

question: Write down the translation of the following verses. • وَلْيَخْشَ الَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافًا خَافُوا عَلَيْهِمْ فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْيَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا • إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَالَ الْيَتَامَى ظُلْمًا إِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ نَارًا وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيرًا
answer: Translation of the first verse (Surah al-Nisa: 9): "And let those (executors and guardians) have the same fear in their minds as they would have for their own, if they had left weak offspring behind. So let them fear Allah and speak right words." Translation of the second verse (Surah al-Nisa: 10): "Verily, those who unjustly eat up the property of orphans, they eat up only a fire into their bellies, and they will be burnt in the blazing Fire!". The first verse urges guardians to treat the orphans with the same care and fear they would wish for their own children, and to speak to them gently and rightly. The second verse warns those who unjustly consume the orphans' property that they are only filling fire into their bellies and will be burnt in the blazing Fire.

question: Write down the rights of the orphans in the light of verse no. 6 of Surah al-Nisa.
answer: Surah al-Nisa, verse 6 ("Wabtalu al-yatama hatta iza balaghu al-nikah...") lays down the rights of the orphans and the conditions and time of handing over their property. The rights and instructions are: (1) Test/try the orphans (as regards their intelligence) until they reach the age of marriage (buloogh); (2) If sound judgement (rushd) — the ability to handle financial and business matters — is found in them, release and hand over their property to them; (3) Do not consume their property wastefully or hastily, fearing that they may grow up and demand it; (4) Among the guardians, whoever is rich should take no wages from the orphans' property, but if he is poor, he may take for himself what is just and reasonable according to his work; (5) When releasing their property to them, take witnesses in their presence to avoid future blame, misunderstanding and quarrels; and (6) Allah is All-Sufficient in taking account. Thus the verse secures both the wealth and the welfare of the orphans and fixes the manner of its safe return.
explanation: Based on the explanation of Surah al-Nisa: 6 with the terms Buloogh and Rushd (book pages 15-16, images 18-19).

question: What do Buloogh and Rushd mean?
answer: Buloogh means to reach the age of marriage (puberty). Rushd means to be able to handle financial and business matters, i.e. sound judgement and the ability to manage and invest property lawfully.
explanation: Definitions given with the explanation of Surah al-Nisa: 6 (book page 15, image 18).

question: What method is instructed in the Holy Quran about handing over the orphans' property to them?
answer: The Holy Quran instructs that the orphans should first be tested until they reach the age of marriage (buloogh); if sound judgement (rushd) and the ability to manage property are found in them, their property should be handed over to them. At the time of handing over, witnesses should be arranged in their presence to avoid any blame, misunderstanding or future quarrel, and the guardian must not consume it wastefully. When this method is followed, the property is returned safely and the orphan's rights are protected.
explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Nisa: 6 (book pages 15-16, images 18-19).

question: What responsibilities of the guardians of the orphans are told in the Holy Quran?
answer: The guardians are responsible for protecting and managing the orphans' property as a trust, not consuming or wasting it, not mixing their own wealth with it, and handing it over to the orphans when they reach puberty and sound judgement. They must also fulfil the orphans' basic needs — catering, clothing, education and training — and speak to them kindly and justly (al-Nisa: 5 and 6); a rich guardian takes no wages while a poor guardian may take only what is just and reasonable.
explanation: From the explanations of Surah al-Nisa: 5 and 6 (book pages 13-16, images 16-19).

question: Write down the translation of any two verses. • يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْبَاطِلِ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً عَنْ تَرَاضٍ مِنْكُمْ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا • مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ أَنَّهُ مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسًا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا
answer: Translation of the first verse (Surah al-Nisa: 29): "O you who believe! Eat not up your property among yourselves unjustly except it be a trade amongst you, by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves (nor kill one another). Surely, Allah is Most Merciful to you." Translation of the second verse (Surah al-Ma'idah: 32): "Because of that We ordained for the Children of Israel that if anyone killed a person not in retaliation of murder, or (and) to spread mischief in the land — it would be as if he killed all mankind; and if anyone saved a life, it would be as if he saved the life of all mankind...". The first verse forbids unlawful consumption of wealth and the killing of one's own self or others. The second verse declares the sanctity of human life, equating the killing of one innocent person with the killing of all humanity and the saving of one life with the saving of all humanity.
explanation: Translations are exactly as given in the lesson (book pages 21 and 23-24, images 24 and 27).

question: Why killing an innocent person is declared killing the whole of humanity?
answer: The Holy Quran (al-Ma'idah: 32) declares that to kill any innocent person — one who neither killed anyone nor spread chaos in the land — is as if he killed the whole of humanity, and to save anyone's life is as if he saved the lives of the whole of humanity. The wisdom behind this is that a person kills only when he breaks up all human relations and loses sympathy for human beings from his heart, seeking only his personal benefit. Such a person disregards the sanctity and honour of human life altogether, and so his crime is regarded as an attack upon the whole of mankind rather than upon one individual. This law was not specified for the Bani Isra'eel only; it lasts for the whole of humanity till the Day of Judgement. It teaches that Islam dislikes bloodshed, chaos and anarchy, and instructs its followers in the principles of peace, patience, forbearance, mutual survival and respect for human beings.
explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Ma'idah: 32 (book pages 23-24, images 26-27).

question: What punishments has been prescribed by the Holy Quran for those who disturb the peace of society?
answer: The Holy Quran (al-Ma'idah: 33-34) prescribes that the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and do mischief in the land is that they shall be killed, or crucified, or their hands and their feet be cut off on the opposite sides, or be exiled from the land. That is their disgrace in this world, and a great torment is theirs in the Hereafter. These four kinds of punishment are stated so that the judge or ruler may decide the nature of every crime by his Ijtihad, keeping in view the objective that bloodshed, robbery, disorder and revolt against Islamic rule are severe crimes and should be prevented. However, the next verse gives an exception: those who repent (make toubah) and come back before they fall into the power of the Muslims — in that case Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful; their rights of Allah may be forgiven, while matters of human rights are settled with the concerned people (return of looted wealth, compensation, retaliation or forgiveness).
explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Ma'idah: 33-34 (book pages 25-26, images 28-29).

question: Write down the meaning of the following words: لَا تَأْكُلُوا ، مُخْتَالًا ، مُسْرِفُونَ ، خِزْيٌ ، تَقْدِرُوا
answer: لَا تَأْكُلُوا — do not eat up / do not devour. مُخْتَالًا — a boastful, proud person. مُسْرِفُونَ — transgressors / those who exceed the limits (set by Allah). خِزْيٌ — disgrace / humiliation. تَقْدِرُوا — you overpower them / get hold of them.
explanation: These words occur in the selected verses (al-Nisa 29, 36 and al-Ma'idah 32, 34) explained in the lesson (images 24-28).

question: Why the protection of the property of orphans is necessary?
answer: The protection of the orphans' property is necessary because wealth is the source of livelihood and survival, and orphans are weak and unable to guard it. Wealth is indispensable for life; any minor negligence can harm the property and its owner. Therefore the Quran commands guardians to protect and manage it honestly, provide for the orphans' needs from it, and hand it over to them when they reach maturity.
explanation: From the explanations of Surah al-Nisa: 5-6 and 10 (book pages 13-19, images 16-22).

question: Write down the meaning of "do not kill yourself".
answer: "Do not kill yourself" (wa la taqtulu anfusakum) means do not kill one another and do not destroy yourselves without any just reason. The murder of an innocent person is unlawful; considering the killing of someone as self-killing denotes that whenever a person kills someone, he will also be killed in retaliation. This verse therefore also prohibits suicide, and self-killing is regarded as worse than being killed in retaliation.
explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Nisa: 29 (book page 22, image 25).

question: What are the unlawful means of earning?
answer: The unlawful means of earning include acquiring and using unlawful things such as pork, liquor and drugs; acquiring even lawful things by unlawful means such as theft, robbery, dacoity, violation of rights, bribery and interest (riba); and earning through lying, fraud, hoarding, black marketing, hedging, gambling, blending and short measuring. All these are forbidden, and wealth earned through transactions made with mutual consent is lawful.
explanation: From the "Eating Up the Property Unlawfully" section explaining Surah al-Nisa: 29 (book page 21, image 24).

question: The unlawful source of income is:
answer: (d) bribery.
explanation: The lesson lists bribery among the unlawful means of earning, while agriculture, industry and business are lawful means (book page 21).
optionsRaw: (a) agriculture (b) industry (c) business (d) bribery

question: Human rights means:
answer: (b) rights of human beings.
explanation: The lesson distinguishes Huqooqullah (rights of Allah) from Huqooq ul Ibad (rights of human beings) (book page 22).
optionsRaw: (a) Rights of Allah (b) rights of human beings (c) rights of animals (d) rights of plants

question: Ibn Sabeel means:
answer: (c) traveller.
explanation: Ibn as-Sabeel (wayfarer/traveller) is listed among those on whom wealth may be spent (book page 22).
optionsRaw: (a) beggar (b) poor (c) traveller (d) neighbour

question: Killing an innocent person is as if killing:
answer: (b) the whole humanity.
explanation: Surah al-Ma'idah: 32 states that killing one innocent person is as if one killed all mankind (book pages 23-24).
optionsRaw: (a) the whole universe (b) the whole humanity (c) the whole animal kingdom (d) the whole family

question: Translate any two verses from the following verses: • هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ • الَّذِينَ إِنْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكَاةَ وَأَمَرُوا بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَنَهَوْا عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَلِلَّهِ عَاقِبَةُ الْأُمُورِ
answer: Translation of the first verse (Surah al-Taubah: 33): "It is He Who has sent His Messenger (Muhammad) with guidance and the religion of truth (Islam), to make it superior over all religions even though the Mushrikun (polytheists, pagans, idolaters, disbelievers in the Oneness of Allah) hate (it)." Translation of the second verse (Surah al-Hajj: 41): "Those (Muslim rulers) who, if We give them power in the land, (they) order for Iqamat-as-Salat (to perform the five compulsory congregational prayers), to pay the Zakat and they enjoin Al-Ma'ruf (Islamic Monotheism and all that Islam orders one to do) and forbid Al-Munkar (disbelief, polytheism and all that Islam has forbidden). And with Allah rests the end of (all) matters." The first verse promises the dominance of Islam over all religions, and the second describes the duties and attributes of the Muslim rulers who are granted authority in the land.
explanation: Translations are exactly as given in the lesson (book pages 29-32, images 32-35).

question: Write the aims, objectives and attributes of the Islamic State mentioned in Surah Al-Hajj verse 41.
answer: Surah al-Hajj, verse 41 describes the aims, objectives and attributes of the Islamic State through the conduct of the Muslim rulers whom Allah grants power in the land. Its aims and objectives are: (1) to establish Salat — ordering Iqamat-as-Salat, i.e. performing the five compulsory congregational prayers (the males in mosques); (2) to pay the Zakat, which is directly related to the economy of society; and (3) to enjoin Al-Ma'ruf (the good — Islamic Monotheism and all that Islam orders) and forbid Al-Munkar (the evil — disbelief, polytheism and all that Islam has forbidden), making the Quran the law of the country in all spheres of life. Its attributes and responsibilities are: to remain steadfast in faith, righteous deeds and worship, abstaining from polytheism; to provide peace and tranquillity to the people; to manage their education, health and livelihood; to create resources of livelihood and make arrangements for the needs of the people; to use their power to spread good and eliminate evil; and to enforce laws and impose punishments on those who cause disorder, so that peace and tranquillity prevail. The verse also reminds that with Allah rests the end of all matters.
explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Hajj: 41 and the responsibilities of the Islamic State (book pages 32-33, images 35-36).

question: A true believer should love "Allah Almighty and His Messenger - Hazrat Muhammad the last of all Prophets the most". Explain in the light of Surah Al-Tawbah verse 24.
answer: Surah al-Taubah, verse 24 says: "Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your kindred, the wealth that you have gained, the commerce in which you fear a decline, and the dwellings in which you delight... are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger, and striving hard and fighting in His Cause, then wait until Allah brings about His Decision (torment). And Allah guides not the people who are Al-Fasiqun (the rebellious, disobedient to Allah)." From this verse it is clear that for a true believer, belief in Allah, love for Allah and His Messenger and doing Jihad in the way of Allah are more important than everything else. No parents, children, spouses, relatives, wealth or home should be dearer to a Muslim than Allah and His Prophet, and no relative's love should stop him from the right path. Faith is the greatest wealth, by which a person gains benefits in this world and prepares himself for the Hereafter. Those who love Allah and His Messenger more than all else and migrate and strive with their life and wealth are honoured in the sight of Allah and are truly successful; but whoever does not love Allah and His Prophet more than everything else cannot be saved from the displeasure of Allah.
explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Taubah: 24 (book pages 28-29, images 31-32).

question: What are the duties of a Muslim leader after gaining power and authority? Explain.
answer: According to Surah al-Hajj: 41, when the believers are given power and authority in the land their duties are as follows: (1) To establish Salat — ordering Iqamat-as-Salat, the five compulsory congregational prayers, so that man's relationship with Allah is strengthened and self-purification is achieved; (2) To pay the Zakat, which is related to the economy of society, and to create resources of livelihood and make arrangements for the needs of the people; (3) To command the good (Amr bil Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (Nahi anil Munkar) — promoting good and virtuous deeds and encouraging those helpful to society, while stopping those responsible for disorder from evildoing, immorality and arrogance, imposing punishments and enforcing laws so that peace and tranquillity prevail; and (4) To make the Quran the law of the country in all spheres of life. In addition, the ruler must remain steadfast in faith, worship and righteous deeds, abstaining from polytheism, and use his power to spread good, eliminate evil and remain firm in fear and danger. In the early Islamic state of Madinah the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the head under the Charter of Medina and was responsible for reconciliation among people, providing peace and tranquillity, and managing their education, health and livelihood.
explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Hajj: 41 and the responsibilities of the Islamic State (book pages 32-33, images 35-36).

question: Write the meanings of the following words: اقْتَرَفْتُمْ ، كَرِهَ ، صَوَامِعُ ، بِيعَةٌ ، مَكَّنَّا
answer: اقْتَرَفْتُمْ — you have earned / committed (the wealth you have gained). كَرِهَ — he/they disliked (hated). صَوَامِعُ — monasteries / abbeys. بِيعَةٌ — churches. مَكَّنَّا — We gave (them) power / control (in the land).
explanation: These words occur in the selected verses (al-Taubah 24, 33 and al-Hajj 40, 41) explained in the lesson (images 31-36).

question: What should be the criterion of the love of Allah Almighty and Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) - the last of all Prophets?
answer: The criterion of the love of Allah and His Messenger is that they should be dearer to a believer than everything else — parents, children, spouses, other relatives, wealth, commerce and homes. No relative or possession should stop him from the right path, and this love should be expressed by striving (Jihad) in the way of Allah. One who does not love Allah and His Prophet more than all else cannot be saved from the displeasure of Allah (al-Taubah: 24).
explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Taubah: 24 (book pages 28-29, images 31-32).

question: Explain the wisdom of Jihad in the light of the Holy Qur'an.
answer: According to Surah al-Hajj: 39-40 and the lesson's explanation, the wisdom of Jihad includes: to defend the Islamic state and society and give permission to fight to those who have been wronged; to help the oppressed; to punish the criminals, the ungrateful and those who break their vows; to protect lives, property, honour, religion and places of worship (mosques, churches, synagogues, monasteries) from mischief; to bring peace and tranquillity in the world; and to strive for the exaltation of the word of Allah Almighty.
explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Hajj: 39-40 (book pages 30-32, images 33-35).

question: How was the condition of Muslims in the Makkan era?
answer: In the Makkan era the condition of the Muslims was very patient and challenging. For the first thirteen years, from the proclamation of the Prophethood in Makkah to the migration to Madinah, both the Muslims and the Holy Prophet (PBUH) suffered severe hardships and oppression at the hands of the opponents. Rather than reacting to these hardships, patience and forbearance were commanded to them, and every kind of retaliation was prevented.
explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Hajj: 39-40 (book page 31, image 34).

question: What is meant by Amr bil Maroof wa Nahi anil Munkar?
answer: Amr bil Maroof wa Nahi anil Munkar means commanding (enjoining) the good and forbidding the evil. "Ma'ruf" (Maroof) means good and virtuous deeds which are considered praiseworthy by all, and "Munkar" means all kinds of evil or wickedness which everyone considers abominable. Good deeds should be promoted in society and people who are helpful to society should be encouraged; while those responsible for the deterioration and disorder of society should be stopped from evildoing, wickedness, immorality and arrogance, with punishments imposed and laws enforced so that peace and tranquillity prevail in society.
explanation: From the "Commanding the good and forbidding the evil" section explaining Surah al-Hajj: 41 (book page 33, image 36).

question: Write down some forms of assistance from Allah Almighty.
answer: The forms of assistance from Allah Almighty mentioned in these verses include: Allah's promise to give victory to the believers who have been wronged (al-Hajj: 39); Allah's protection of the believers against the oppressors who are the enemies of Islam (al-Hajj: 38); Allah's granting of power and authority in the land to the believers (al-Hajj: 41); Allah's help to those who help His cause — "Truly, Allah will help those who help His (Cause)" (al-Hajj: 40); and the promise that He will make the religion of truth (Islam) superior over all other religions (al-Taubah: 33).
explanation: From the explanations of Surah al-Hajj: 39-41 and Surah al-Taubah: 33 (book pages 30-33, images 33-36).
